claims.text: TCA overdose: dysrhythmias, severe hypotension, convulsions and CNS depression or coma; QRS axis or width changes are key signs of toxicity.
claims.quote: Critical manifestations of overdose include: cardiac dysrhythmias, severe hypotension, convulsions, and CNS depression, including coma. Changes in the electrocardiogram, particularly in, QRS axis or width, are clinically significant indicators of tricyclic antidepressant toxicity.

claims.text: Get an ECG, start cardiac monitoring and observe for at least six hours;
claims.quote: Obtain an ECG and immediately initiate cardiac monitoring. Protect the patient's airway, establish an intravenous line and initiate gastric decontamination. A minimum of six hours of observation

claims.text: a limb-lead QRS of 0.10 seconds or more may best show severity; give IV sodium bicarbonate to keep serum pH at 7.45 to 7.55.
claims.quote: A maximal limb-lead QRS duration of ≥0.10 seconds may be the best indication of the severity of the overdose. Intravenous sodium bicarbonate should be used to maintain the serum pH in the range of 7.45 to 7.55.

claims.text: Type 1A and 1C antiarrhythmics are generally contraindicated.
claims.quote: Type 1 A and 1 C antiarrhythmics are generally contraindicated

claims.text: CYP2D6 inhibitors (eg, quinidine, cimetidine) can make a patient stable on a TCA abruptly toxic;
claims.quote: An individual who is stable on a given dose of TCA may become abruptly toxic when given one of these inhibiting drugs as concomitant therapy. The drugs that inhibit cytochrome P450 2D6 include some that are not metabolized by the enzyme (quinidine; cimetidine)
claims.locator: Precautions › Drug Interactions › Drugs Metabolized by P450 2D6

claims.text: the combination may need lower doses of the TCA or the other drug.
claims.quote: Concomitant use of tricyclic antidepressants with drugs that can inhibit cytochrome P450 2D6 may require lower doses than usually prescribed for either the tricyclic antidepressant or the other drug.
claims.locator: Precautions › Drug Interactions › Drugs Metabolized by P450 2D6
